# Evri invests £1.3m in new Gloucester parcel depot

 October 12, 2026 Mark Salisbury Filed under: Last Mile Deliveries, Logistics, Manufacturer News, News, Newsletter, Secondary News, Third-Party Logistics (3PL) 

Evri Group has opened a new £1.3 million depot in Gloucester, expanding its parcel delivery network across the South West and creating dozens of permanent jobs.

The new facility at Indurent Park Gloucester in Quedgeley replaces the company’s previous operation in Tewkesbury, which had reached capacity. The investment will help Evri manage rising parcel volumes, strengthen regional operations and improve its ability to meet customer demand.

The depot has created 38 permanent roles across warehouse, driving, operational and management functions. The investment also supports local employment while providing additional capacity for the growing logistics business.

Image: Evri

# Savona Foodservice Unveils £3 Million London Depot Expansion to Support Growth and Innovation

Savona Foodservice has officially opened the doors to its new London distribution depot, marking an exciting new chapter for our business and a significant investment in our future across London and the South East.

As our customer base and product range have continued to grow, so has the need for greater capacity. The 50,000 square foot site has given us a larger, more efficient facility designed to support our customers today while preparing us for future growth.

At the heart of the expansion is a significant increase in warehouse capacity, including over c. 2,000 additional freezer and chiller pallet spaces. This means greater product availability and the ability to offer an even broader range of products.

# GLS expands fulfilment offering with new centre in Denmark

GLS expands its fulfilment footprint with a new purpose-built centre in Kolding, marking the company's entry into fulfilment services in Denmark.

 07 October 2026 - 2 min 

- GLS Denmark has broken ground on a new fulfilment centre in Kolding, marking its entry into fulfilment services.
- The 5,000-square-metre facility is expected to be ready for use ahead of the 2027 peak season and can be scaled to 15,000 square metres to accommodate further growth.
- The investment supports GLS Group’s ambition to connect parcel delivery and fulfilment in a broader end-to-end offering for customers.

Amsterdam, 6 October 2026 – GLS is expanding its fulfilment capabilities with a new purpose-built centre in Kolding, Denmark. The new facility will mark GLS Denmark's entry into fulfilment services and support the Group's development of connected logistics solutions that combine parcel delivery with storage and order processing.

# DSV stärker paketdistributionen i Stockholm med ny terminal i Spånga

DSV fortsätter att utveckla sin kapacitet och öppnar en ny paketterminal i Lunda, Spånga. Den nya terminalen ska hantera paketdistribution i Storstockholm och skapar förutsättningar för kortare ledtider genom utökad geografisk kapacitet.

Den nya paketterminalen omfattar cirka 8 000 kvadratmeter och har kapacitet att hantera upp till 10 000 paket i timmen. Etableringen är en viktig del i DSVs fortsatta utveckling av distributionsnätverket och stärker företagets förmåga att möta efterfrågan på paketleveranser i Stockholmsregionen.

”Stockholm är en mycket viktig marknad för oss. Med den nya paketterminalen utökar vi vår kapacitet i regionen och kan hantera paketdistribution över ett större geografiskt område. Etableringen är ett viktigt steg i den fortsatta utvecklingen av vårt distributionsnätverk och ger oss en plattform för att möta framtida efterfrågan, säger Tomas Johansson, vd för DSV Road AB.

## LTL carrier’s North American terminal count reaches 300 

 Todd Maiden 

· Thursday, October 01, 2026 

 XPO expanded its North American footprint to 300 terminals following the addition of new service centers in Missouri and Arizona. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Less-than-truckload carrier XPO announced Thursday that it has added new locations in Arizona and Missouri, increasing its terminal count to 300 across North America.

A new 51,000-square-foot facility in Mesa, Arizona has 86 dock doors and over 100 employees. The terminal gives XPO (NYSE: XPO) needed capacity to serve the Phoenix market, where it already operates a freight assembly center. The region is experiencing an increase in demand given recent industrial investments and growing cross-border trade with Mexico.

A 13,000-square-foot terminal in Cameron, Missouri (approximately 50 miles north of Kansas City) has 32 dock doors and over 30 employees. It sits near the intersection of I-35 and U.S. 36, serving both north-south and east-west freight corridors.

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

# Gofo parcel network quickly mushrooms in 2026

## New Dallas hub offers more room, automation to handle volume growth as peak season approaches 

 Eric Kulisch 

· Thursday, August 27, 2026 

 Gofo’s new Dallas warehouse is twice the size of the previous facility, allowing it to process more parcels while improving efficiency. (Photo: Gofo) 

Parcel delivery startup Gofo has doubled the capacity of its Dallas processing center after moving into a new building and installing automated sortation equipment, as it races other regional carriers to build national scale.

The larger terminal comes on line ahead of the peak season rush, allowing the company to absorb greater volume in the central United States rather than adding temporary facilities mid-season. Gofo says it expects parcel volume to jump 50% above normal weekly levels during the period between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
